descriptionChirho: A proper noun designating Hazael, the Aramean king of Damascus who reigned in the mid-9th century BCE. The name means 'El sees' (Assyrian Hazailu). He appears throughout 1 Kings 19, 2 Kings 8-13, 2 Chronicles 22, and Amos 1:4 as a key political and military figure who oppressed Israel. All occurrences across the auto-clustered senses refer to the same historical individual; the separate clusters arose from minor orthographic variation (the longer spelling with he, transliteration differences such as Hazael vs. Chazael vs. Khazael) and different prepositional prefixes (bare, with waw, with lamed), none of which reflect distinct senses.
